newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hoogovens, UGB seal 4.25 bln Bfr alliance.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens, UGB seal 4.25 bln Bfr alliance.

text.p: Dutch steel maker Hoogovens and privately owned Belgian steel firm Usines Gustave Boel (UGB) formally signed a 50/50 joint venture on Friday.

Under the terms of the link-up 4.25 billion Belgian francs ($121.8 million) in fresh funds will be injected into UGB, of which Hoogovens will pay 2.25 billion francs, the companies said in a statement released at a news conference in Brussels.
The steel sector investment company of Belgium's Walloon region, where IGB is located, will invest 500 million francs and UGB's present shareholders, mainly the Boel family, will pay the remainder.
The 50/50 joint venture to be formed by Hoogovens and the present shareholders of UGB will own 100 percent of UGB and of steel plant Fabrique de Fer de Maubeuge.
Hoogovens will supply semi-products to UGB's rolling mills. "The market pBositions of UGB and Hoogovens can thus be optimised to the benefit of their customers," the companies said.
The Dutch company has said previously it is not interested by UGB's crude steel production.
The definitive closure of the deal was pending approval "by the appropriate authorities," the companies said, without elaborating.
